title: Fall Back! Daylight Saving Time Ends on November 1
summary:
Get ready to fall back! On November 1, 2026, many North Americans will turn their clocks back one hour, adding 60 minutes to their weekend. That simple action marks the end of Daylight Saving Time (DST), which began on March 8, 2026. The change shifts more sunlight back into the morning, making it a little easier to wake up for school or work during the shorter winter days ahead.

DST was first introduced during World War I. In 1916, the German Empire moved clocks forward by one hour to reduce the need for artificial lighting and save fuel for the war effort, and the US and Britain soon followed. After the war, the countries returned to standard time, then reinstated DST during World War II.

When the war ended in 1945, US officials canceled DST nationwide but allowed states and districts to keep it, each with its own dates. The result was a confusing patchwork - by 1965, Iowa alone had 23 different sets of DST dates! The Uniform Time Act of 1966 ended the confusion by setting the same "spring forward" and "fall back" dates for the entire country, but the law was not mandatory, so Hawaii, most of Arizona and several US territories chose not to take part.

The dates have moved since then. In 1986, President Ronald Reagan shifted the start to the first Sunday in April, and the Energy Policy Act of 2005 moved it to the second Sunday in March and extended the end to the first Sunday in November, a schedule used since 2007. About 70 countries around the world observe DST, though experts say the twice-a-year changes can disrupt the body's sleep-wake cycle, leading to fatigue and reduced concentration.

Several US states have passed laws to stay on DST year-round, but those laws cannot take effect unless federal law changes. The House passed the Sunshine Protection Act, which would make DST permanent nationwide, by a vote of 308-117 in July 2026, but the Senate has yet to approve it. So for now, unless you live somewhere that skips DST, enjoy the bonus hour on November 1!
why_it_matters: Clock changes affect sleep, school and travel for millions of people twice a year. The debate over keeping one time all year is still unresolved because state laws cannot take effect unless federal law changes.

keywords.explanation: Daylight Saving Time is the period when clocks are set one hour ahead of standard time.
Standard time is the normal local time used when Daylight Saving Time is not in effect.
A patchwork here means a confusing mix of different rules in different places.
Mandatory means something must be done because a rule or law requires it.
Fatigue is a feeling of being very tired and low in energy.

background_read: Daylight Saving Time is a system that moves clocks forward in spring and back in autumn to shift daylight between morning and evening.
It began as a way to save fuel by reducing the need for artificial lighting during wartime.
Because time rules affect school, work and travel, a whole country needs shared dates instead of many different local ones.
Some places choose not to observe Daylight Saving Time, and changing the national rule requires a change in federal law.
